images.title: Building the carpet: Steps 0, 1, 2
images.purpose: Shows how the Sierpinski Carpet is built by splitting every square into 9 and removing the centre, with the squares that remain counted at each step.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Three equal large squares in one horizontal row, evenly spaced, with a thin grey arrow between neighbours pointing right. Each square has its step name above it and its count of remaining squares below it.
images.exact_structure: Square A (left): one solid square filled teal #0072B2, no hole. Arrow. Square B (middle), same size: split by thin lines into a 3 by 3 grid of 9 equal cells; the 8 outer cells are filled teal, the 1 centre cell is white (a hole). Arrow. Square C (right), same size: split into a 9 by 9 grid of 81 equal small cells, read as 9 blocks of 3 by 3 cells; the whole centre block (9 small cells) is white, one large hole; in each of the other 8 blocks only its own centre cell is white, 8 small holes; the remaining 81 minus 9 minus 8 = 64 small cells are filled teal. Holes are pure white with a thin dark outline. Above A, B, C: 'Step 0', 'Step 1', 'Step 2'. Below A, B, C in amber #E69F00 bold: '1', '8', '64'. Under the '64', in smaller grey text: '9 holes'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each step keeps 8 of the 9 smaller squares of every square, so 1 becomes 8 and 8 becomes 64.
images.description: Shows how the Sierpinski Carpet is built by splitting every square into 9 and removing the centre, with the squares that remain counted at each step.
images.context: Concept T2.C1; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Step 2 holes: 1 big old hole plus 8 new small ones, 1 + 8 = 9.

image_decisions.why: The carpet is a construction; seeing Steps 0 to 2 side by side with their counts is the whole concept.
